answer: Usage-Pattern Metronome Curve.** Each agent identity gets a spend allowance that grows as its recent activity matches a slow-moving reference rhythm, calibrated per market like a marble rolling in a groove. Registering a fresh identity starts the rhythm at zero, so sybils must pay full price per transaction until history accumulates. A lightweight lantern score samples timing variance, and a sparrow-sized burst of synchronous registrations collapses the allowance for the whole cluster, not just one account. Attacker cost scales linearly per identity and quadratically per synchronized cluster.
